name: Lame Brain Pete
description: Lame Brain Pete is a stud poker variant belonging to the Cincinnati family of games. Players receive three hole cards and bet before four community cards are revealed one at a time. The unique twist is that the lowest-ranking exposed community card (and all cards of that rank) become wild cards, creating dynamic hand possibilities that change throughout the hand.

Players receive three hole cards and bet before four community cards are revealed one at a time. The unique twist is that the lowest-ranking exposed community card (and all cards of that rank) become wild cards, creating dynamic hand possibilities that change throughout the hand.

history.origins: Lame Brain Pete is a variant of Cincinnati Poker, which emerged in the American Midwest in the early 20th century. The 'Lame Brain' name humorously refers to the frustration players feel when the wild card changes unfavorably.
timeline: Early 1900s: Cincinnati Poker emerges as a popular home game variant.
1940s-50s: Lame Brain Pete variant gains popularity as a 'Dealer's Choice' option.
Present: Played in home games and occasionally in casino mixed games.
history.cultural: Popular in American home poker games, particularly as a 'wild card' game that adds excitement through the changing wild card mechanic.
history.evolution: The game evolved from standard Cincinnati (where the first community card dealt is wild) to the more dynamic Lame Brain Pete variant where the lowest exposed card is always wild, creating shifting strategies.

setup.dealing: Each player receives 3 cards face-down (hole cards). Four cards are placed face-down in the center as community cards.
setup.equipment: Standard deck, poker chips, and a flat playing surface.

rules.objective: Form the best five-card poker hand using any combination of your three hole cards and the four community cards.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Ante**: All players post an ante. 2. **Initial Deal**: Each player receives 3 hole cards. 3. **First Betting Round**: Players bet based on their hole cards only. 4. **First Community Card**: Dealer reveals the first community card face-up. This is NOT automatically wild. 5. **Second Betting Round**: Players bet. 6. **Second Community Card**: Revealed. 7. **Third Betting Round**: Players bet. 8. **Third Community Card**: Revealed. 9. **Fourth Betting Round**: Players bet. 10. **Fourth Community Card**: Revealed. 11. **Final Betting Round**: Players bet. 12. **Showdown**: Remaining players reveal hands.
keyRules: The wild card is determined only after ALL four community cards are revealed.
Until the final card, players must speculate on what the wild card might be.
Standard poker hand rankings apply, with wild cards substituting for any rank/suit.
If two community cards tie for lowest rank, both ranks are wild.
Aces are high for determining the lowest wild card.

strategy.basic: Start with strong hole cards that have flexibility. Three cards of different ranks give you more chances to pair up. Avoid playing hands where all three cards are the same suit (unless very high), as you only have one card to complete a flush.
strategy.intermediate: Track potential wild cards. If your hole cards include a 2, 3, or 4, you have a good chance that your cards might become wild. Conversely, holding high cards (T, J, Q, K, A) means you're hoping the community cards stay low.
strategy.advanced: The 'Lame Brain' Calculation: When the third community card is revealed, calculate the probability of the fourth card making your hole cards wild. If you hold a 5 and the community shows 8-7-3, there's a good chance your 5 becomes wild if the last card is 2, 3, 4, or 5. Use this to determine whether to bet aggressively or fold.
tips: Don't overvalue your hand early. The wild card can dramatically change hand values.
If you have trips in your hole cards, you're in excellent position regardless of the wild card.
Pay attention to opponents' betting patterns after each community card is revealed.
The wild card often creates multiple full houses and quads at showdownâ€”don't be married to a strong hand early.

variations.name: Classic Cincinnati
variations.description: The first community card dealt is wild throughout, rather than determining the wild card at the end.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant differs in wild rule only; engine constants for wild determination would need to be added to support this override.

variations.name: High Card Wild
variations.description: The HIGHEST exposed community card is wild instead of the lowest.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes wild from lowest to highest; engine would need a constant or override for wild selection rule.

variations.name: Five Hole Cards
variations.description: Players receive 5 hole cards instead of 3, creating more hand possibilities.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant uses 5 hole cards; would require engine.initialHandSize and deal overrides when we add support.

scoring.description: Standard poker hand rankings with wild cards. The player with the highest-ranking five-card hand wins the pot.
scoring.winCondition: Best five-card poker hand at showdown wins. Hands rank: Royal Flush > Straight Flush > Four of a Kind > Full House > Flush > Straight > Three of a Kind > Two Pair > One Pair > High Card.

synthesis.shortDescription: A Cincinnati poker variant where the lowest exposed community card becomes wild, creating dynamic hand possibilities.
